summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for August 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

eli5.summary: It is like a monthly count of how many cars used each road, written down so people can see which roads are busy.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in august 1973
how many packets did the arpanet carry in august 1973
which arpanet host sent the most packets in august 1973
subtitle: BBN's table of how many packets each ARPANET host sent in August 1973.

tldr.problem: ARPANET sites wanted to know how much traffic each host was generating.
tldr.mechanism: BBN-NET attached a Host Throughput Summary for August 1973, listing packets output per host, split into internode and intranode traffic.
tldr.outcome: The report gives monthly totals, daily averages and a ratio of packets to messages. RFC 579 later updated it.

today: RFC 566 is a one-month data report, and RFC 579 updates it. It has no protocol content to be current or outdated.

sections.title: What the Report Is
sections.content:
RFC 566, from A. McKenzie of BBN-NET and dated 4 September 1973, is a cover note: "Attached are the Hosts traffic statistics for the month of August 1973." The header says it updates RFC 556.

The rest is the attached table, titled HOST THROUGHPUT SUMMARY (PACKETS OUTPUT).
sections.eli5: A person at BBN sent around a monthly scoreboard of network traffic.

sections.title: How to Read the Table
sections.content:
Each row is a host at a site such as UCLA, SRI or MIT. For each host the table gives internode packets, intranode packets and a total. Sites with several hosts also get a subtotal, the average daily internode packets, and the number of days counted, which is 31 for August.

BELV, ABER and LBL are listed as having had no traffic.
sections.eli5: Each line says how many messages a computer sent to other places and how many it kept close to home.

sections.title: Network Totals
sections.content:
The network-wide totals are 99009940 internode packets and 37732470 intranode packets. The daily averages are 3193869 and 1217177, and the average per node-day is 86321 and 31897.

PACKETS/MESSAGES (INTERNODE) is again 1.07. Among the listed hosts, ISI HOST 1 had the most internode packets, 14683780.
sections.eli5: The bottom adds everything up so you can see how busy the whole network was that month.

references.text: RFC 556, the earlier traffic statistics report that this RFC's header says it updates.
